description:
James Braidwood (1800–1861) was a Scottish firefighter who was the first Master of Engines in the world's first municipal fire service in Edinburgh in 1824. He was also the first director of the London Fire Engine Establishment and is credited with the development of the modern municipal fire service. His methods are still used today. His life was claimed in the fires that burned for two weeks at Cotton's wharf, Tooley Street.

Braidwood has a pedestal memorial headstone of 'white stone' (as described in the book about Abney Park) - it is likely a limestone. This was painted in the past, either at the time of installation (or perhaps the last burial in the grave) there is flaking white paint present, as well as faded blacking in the lettering. At some point in the last 25 - 30 years, a well-meaning person took it upon themselves to re-black the lettering without permission (or knowledge of cemetery staff) - this did not improve the headstone. 

Further research has revealed that the headstone was re-discovered in 1981 and was at that time painted with Dulux masonry paint. An image on the Historic England dated 2003 suggests that it was repainted at this time.

This proposal it to restore the memorial to it's original state. (There are no historical images of the memorial.) 
1/ a small sample of paint will be removed for testing to ensure like-for-like replacement
2/ the paint will be non-invasively removed on all four sides
3/ the stone surface will cleaned
4/ the white paint will be replaced
4/ the black lettering will be re-painted

As pedestal headstones of the period were sometimes whitewashed or limewashed a decision on the final finish is pending. We would like to see the stone restored to it's original state.
